items.title: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
items.summary: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO The Kremlin is getting closer to opening its 'new eye' on Europe. Construction of a towering radar complex is almost complete in Russia's highly militarized exclave of Kaliningrad, according to reports From above, the three radiating arms of the sprawling facility – each more than 500 meters long – look like some sort of alien lifeform has left its mark on an otherwise undisturbed stretch of forested nature reserve. You could actually compare it to a landing platform or launch pad for Moscow's massive intelligence-gathering network While Russia has not confirmed it is building the structure, security expert Vaidotas Malinionis said the radar will be so big, it will be able to see beyond the earth's curvature.

items.title: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
items.summary: Armed police officers on patrol outside Sydney's Luna Park Heavily-armed police officers have started patrolling Sydney's streets, as part of heightened security measures following last year's deadly shooting at Bondi Beach The Armed Response Command (ARC) will see specially trained officers in busy tourist areas carrying long-arm rifles – an unfamiliar sight for most residents New South Wales police say the officers will also patrol major events like sports matches and places of worship "to prevent, deter and rapidly respond to serious threats, including active armed offender incidents" Fifteen people - including a 10-year-old girl – were killed in December when two gunmen opened fire on an event marking the Jewish festival of Hanukkah at the popular beach The attack was Australia's worst mass shooting in almost three decades and prompted sweeping gun law reforms and a crackdown on hate speech One resident told ABC news that the sight of armed police was "unnerving" "They are just everywhere.

items.title: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
items.summary: There is no vaccine for this strain of the virus, but clinical trials are under way More than 5,000 people have died from an ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, government data shows Eight of 26 provinces are now affected, with more than 10,300 confirmed cases The outbreak, which started in May, became the country's deadliest in its history in August, public health officials said.

items.title: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
items.summary: The training comes as Ethiopia faces continued fighting in parts of the northern Tigray region Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has put his cabinet ministers and other senior government officials through military training, saying armed forces discipline can help build stronger leaders and advance the country's development Photos shared by him on social media show him taking part in military exercises alongside ministers, deputy ministers and heads of government institutions at the Hurso military training centre The move is unusual in Ethiopia, where senior civilian government officials are rarely seen undergoing military training Those taking part include Speaker of the House of Federation Muferiat Kamil, Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa and Health Minister Mekdes Daba It is unclear when the training began or how long it is expected to last In his post, the prime minister, who is known as Abiy, said Ethiopia's ambition to achieve universal prosperity required its leadership to be physically fit, morally strong and intellectually capable He said military institutions offered…
